constraint_decided_it: P24 transferred title of (E8 -> E18) and P30 transferred custody of (E10 -> E18) are both quantified 'many to many, necessary (1,n:0,n)', so every E8 and every E10 must carry one; B instantiates both, A names neither. E96 Purchase (subclass of E8: 'transfers of legal ownership ... where the transferring party is completely compensated by the payment of a monetary amount ... begins with the contract ... ends with the fulfilment of all contractual obligations') is the more specific class for a paid auction sale; B raises and defers it, A never mentions it. Nothing in domain/range separated the core answer: P22/P23 (E8 -> E39) and P28/P29 (E10 -> E39) are correctly applied by both, and both correctly refuse the second E8 because E8's scope note is legal ownership only while E10's covers 'the physical custody or the legal responsibility for the physical custody'.
better_modelling: One E96 Purchase (subclass of E8) with P23 engineer, P22 phone bidder, P24 the instruments, its temporal extent running from the fall of the hammer to the settlement ten days later (E96: 'ends with the fulfilment of all contractual obligations' -- this is what the ten-day hold actually is, and neither answer used it); plus two E10 Transfer of Custody events with P28/P29/P30 (engineer -> auction house, auction house -> courier), the consignment leg qualified with P2 has type per E10's scope note ('In the event that only a single kind of transfer of custody occurs, either the legal responsibility for the custody or the actual physical possession ... this difference should be expressed using the property P2 has type'); the auction house attached to the Purchase by P14 with a P14.1 role, with the caveat that Issue 488 was closed deferring 'acting at the behest of another' to CRMsoc, so no CRMbase property expresses agency for the consignor.
reasoning: Both answers reach the same axis split -- one title transfer, two custody transfers -- and it is the split the CRM prescribes: E8's scope note confines it to legal ownership, E10's covers legal responsibility for custody, and the published E10 examples (von Merian -> Auction House Heldevier 'for the purpose of sale'; Mrs. Fitzherbert, Parke-Bernet -> Knoedler, added under Issue 516 from the Getty Provenance Index, t1469) model consignment legs as custody, never as a second Acquisition. B is better on CRM grounds because it satisfies the necessary quantification of P24 and P30, invokes the P2 has type qualification E10's scope note demands, and correctly reports Issue 488 / t1345 as unsettled for 'acted on behalf of'; A omits P24 and P30 entirely and presents Doerr's mediator remark as settled practice. Both are suboptimal for the same reason: E96 Purchase is the more specific applicable class and neither adopts it. Citation checks: A's Doerr quote is real (t0914 msg 7, 'an instance of Purchase, which is also an instance of Acquisition, can have additional parties "caried out by" "in the role of" "Mediator"?' -- A silently elides the Purchase framing that would have pointed it at E96) and its t1540 claim is verbatim accurate (Sanderson: 'the auction of the lot is not the same entity as the E8 acquisition'); B's t1376 quote is verbatim but its status label is false -- Issue 475's register accepted only the scope note and 'decided to rework the examples in a separate issue', the Aphrodite/Sotheby's example never entered 7.1.3 or 7.3.2, so 'accepted homework example' is unsupported even though the conclusion it supports is right.
